decisions.reason: Correctly locates the partial/runningCalls/turnEnds reads in Pet.tsx with valid citations and identifies them as breaking surfaces, but the projection story is wrong: it claims partial is not covered by the compatibility projection while running/runningCalls/turnEnds are served via invented flags.* fields. The frozen A1-03 note says nodes/partial/runningCalls/turnEnds are all still readable through views.get('chat')?.legacy, and the report never mentions that legacy projection or the follow-up views/timeline migration.

Locates the running read and keeps the useSession call form, but asserts the compatibility projection can keep emitting running for one cycle (s.flags.running), directly contradicting the reference which states lifecycle fields like running are not in the projection and must go through the useSession seat. The report draws no chat-legacy vs session-lifecycle seat distinction; its taxonomy inverts the sealed facts.

It cites the Pet.tsx ConversationSnapshot import but its proposed fix imports SessionSnapshot from @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime/client — a package removed in alpha.1 per A1-25/API-10. It never repoints Context/ClientContext to scoped @deepseek-ai/cordis, never moves snapshot types to their owning packages, and never addresses the package.json dsh.client.inject entry that still lists dsh-client-runtime and must drop it.

Locates the scoped registration in index.ts, explains the slots+conversation ordering edge (register into an undeclared slot throws), and preserves the slot name, id, order, and effect-wrapped lifetime. However it does not repoint the ClientContext import from the removed runtime package, nor discuss the ui-renderer/client Context augmentation via type-only imports or service ownership after the package split.

The card mapping invents DSH-0.1.2-A1-01 through A1-06 with plausible descriptions but never ties the changes to DSH-0.1.2-A1-03, and never mentions the valid A1-25 package-removal card even though the report keeps importing from the removed runtime package. Its projection-vs-immediate split is also inverted for running/partial, so the separation requirement is not met.
